Vishnusharman.description: The narrator and teacher who tells the stories to the princes.

Cloudy.description: Cloudy, the crow-king, leads the crows and seeks counsel on how to deal with the owl enemy.

Foe-Crusher.description: Foe-Crusher, the owl-king, is the leader of the owls, rival of Cloudy, and wages war against the crows.

Live-Again.description: One of Cloudy's five ancestral counselors, advocates for making peace with the enemy.

Live-Well.description: One of Cloudy's counselors, advises fighting against the enemy.

Live-Along.description: One of Cloudy's counselors, recommends a change of base rather than peace or war.

Live-On.description: One of Cloudy's counselors, suggests entrenchment and defense within the fortress.

LiveLong.description: One of Cloudy's counselors who recommends forming alliances or changing bases.

Live-Strong.description: An ancient and farsighted counselor of Cloudy's race, advocates duplicity and the use of spies.

Narada.description: A sage referenced by Live-Strong as a source of knowledge about royal functionaries.

Fight-Firm.description: A king mentioned in a proverb and as a recipient of Narada's advice.

Bhima.description: A legendary hero from the Mahabharata who defeated his foe Kichaka through deception.

Book III.description: The third book of the Panchatantra, titled 'Crows and Owls.'

Earth-Base.description: A city in the southern country where the story is set.

banyan.description: A large, sacred fig tree native to India, often associated with longevity and shelter.

April.description: A month mentioned as a suitable time for invasion according to the text.

November.description: A month mentioned as a suitable time for invasion according to the text.

retinue.description: A group of attendants or followers accompanying an important person.

habitation.description: A place of residence or dwelling.

entrenchment.description: The act of fortifying or defending a position, often by digging trenches.

duplicity.description: Deceitfulness or double-dealing in speech or conduct.

foemen.description: Archaic term for enemies or foes.

gyneceum.description: The women's quarters in a palace or large household.

superintendent.description: A person who manages or oversees a particular department or operation.

concierge.description: An attendant or caretaker, especially in a palace or large household.

star-gazer.description: An astrologer or astronomer, often consulted for omens or advice.

quartermaster.description: An officer responsible for the supply of food, equipment, and accommodations.

geisha.description: A female entertainer, though in this context likely refers to a court performer or attendant.

purveyor.description: A supplier, especially of food or provisions.

professor.description: A learned person or teacher, especially in a royal court.

life-guard.description: A bodyguard or protector, especially for a king or important person.

counselor.description: An advisor, especially to a king or leader.

functionary.description: An official who performs a specific function or duty, often in government or administration.

doggerel.description: Comic or irregular verse, often used for mnemonic or illustrative purposes.

moat.description: A deep, wide ditch surrounding a fortress, typically filled with water for defense.

shaft.description: An arrow or spear; in this context, a weapon for defense.

sally.description: A sudden charge out of a besieged place against the enemy.

Garuda.description: A mythical bird and king of the birds, traditionally the mount of Vishnu; here, he is described as inattentive to the birds' needs.

Vishnu.description: A major Hindu deity; King Prithu is considered an incarnation of this preserver god.

owl.description: Owl (or owls) refers to the bird proposed by the bird-clans as their new king due to his venerable appearance, one of whom is chosen as king.

crow.description: A clever and shrewd bird who interrupts the coronation and questions the wisdom of making the owl king.

swans.description: A type of bird mentioned among the bird-clans, regarded as eminent.

cranes.description: A type of bird present at the gathering.

nightingales.description: Birds known for their song, included among the bird-clans.

peacocks.description: Colorful birds present at the assembly.

plovers.description: A type of bird mentioned in the gathering.

demoiselles.description: A type of crane, present at the gathering.

sheldrakes.description: A type of waterfowl mentioned by the crow as eminent.

lion-throne.description: A ceremonial throne prepared for the coronation of the bird king.

White-Robe.description: A reference to a particular class or group of priests, possibly Jain monks, known for their white attire.

anointing.description: The ritual act of applying oil or other substances to a person, especially during a coronation.

oblation.description: A religious offering, often of food or grain, made as part of a ritual.

lustration.description: A ceremonial purification by means of water or other substances.

parched grain.description: Grain that has been roasted or dried, often used in rituals.

potash.description: A substance (potassium carbonate) used in rituals to purify or consecrate a space.

consecrated.description: Made or declared sacred, especially through a religious ceremony.

mustard.description: White mustard seeds, commonly used in Indian rituals for purification.

caw.description: The harsh cry of a crow.

monarch.description: A king or supreme ruler, used here for the bird chosen as king.

holiday drums.description: Drums played during festivals or ceremonial occasions.

wreaths.description: Garlands of flowers used for decoration or ritual purposes.

twigs.description: Small branches, often used in rituals.

Four-Tusk.description: The elephant-king who leads and protects his herd during a time of drought.

Victory.description: A clever rabbit who devises the plan to save the rabbits from the elephants.

Block-Snout.description: The rabbit-king who trusts Victory to act as envoy to the elephants.

Moon.description: Referred to as the 'blessed Moon,' a deity who is said to protect the rabbits and whose lake is threatened by the elephants.

Lake of the Moon.description: A beautiful lake near a hermitage, sacred to the Moon and home to many rabbits.

Seven Sages.description: A reference to the constellation of the seven great sages (Saptarishi) in Indian astronomy, seen reflected in the lake.

hermitage.description: A secluded residence, often for religious retreat or ascetic living.

ichor-juice.description: A mythical or poetic term for the fragrant liquid that oozes from the temples of elephants.

bosom.description: An archaic term for the chest or heart, often used figuratively for protection or affection.

peradventure.description: An archaic word meaning 'perhaps' or 'by chance.'

nuncio.description: An envoy or messenger, especially one representing a sovereign or religious authority.

envoy.description: A representative or messenger, often sent on a diplomatic mission.

obeisance.description: A gesture or act of respect or submission, such as a bow.

digits.description: In this context, refers to the divisions or phases of the moon.

umpire.description: A person chosen to settle disputes; in this context, a judge or arbitrator.

Speedy.description: A rabbit who occupies the partridge's old nest and becomes involved in a dispute over its ownership.

Curd-Ear.description: A tomcat who pretends to be a holy ascetic and is chosen to judge the dispute between the rabbit and the partridge.

Ganges.description: A sacred river in India, often referenced in Hindu tradition and literature.

Brahman.description: Brahman (plural: Brahmans) refers to a member of the priestly caste in Hindu society, often depicted as a learned and pious individual, worthy of straightforward conduct.

partridge.description: A type of bird, often featured in Indian fables.

cisterns.description: Large storage tanks for water, commonly used in Indian villages.

conundrums.description: Riddles or puzzles, often used in storytelling.

consecrated tradition.description: A phrase referring to established religious or legal customs.

penance.description: Voluntary self-punishment or religious discipline to express repentance.

self-denial.description: The act of denying oneself pleasures or desires, often for religious reasons.

pharisaic.description: Hypocritically self-righteous or sanctimonious, originally referring to the Pharisees.

hermeneutic.description: Related to the interpretation of sacred texts.

exegesis.description: Critical explanation or interpretation of a text, especially scripture.

regal anointing.description: A ceremonial act of crowning or consecrating a king.

expedients.description: Means or methods used to achieve a particular end, often with a sense of cleverness or resourcefulness.

Friendly.description: A Brahman who maintains the sacred fire and is the main character of the story, tricked by three rogues.

three rogues.description: A group of three cunning men who trick the Brahman into abandoning his goat.

sacred fire.description: A ritual fire maintained by Brahmans for religious ceremonies.

sacrificer.description: One who performs or sponsors a religious sacrifice.

victim.description: An animal offered as a sacrifice in a religious ritual.

offering.description: A ritual gift, often food or an animal, presented to a deity.

new moon.description: A lunar phase significant in Hindu ritual timing.

plump.description: Well-fed or fat; in this context, refers to the goat's suitability for sacrifice.

unconventional.description: Not conforming to established customs or practices.

defile.description: To make unclean or impure, especially in a ritual sense.

impute.description: To attribute or ascribe, especially something undesirable.

pet.description: A domesticated animal kept for companionship; here, used to refer to a calf.

lunar fast.description: A religious fast observed according to the lunar calendar.

purify.description: To cleanse from ritual or spiritual impurity.

ass.description: An archaic term for a donkey.

populace.description: The general public or common people.

roguish.description: Characteristic of a rogue; playfully mischievous or deceitful.

Haughty.description: A prodigious black snake living in an ant-hill who is attacked and killed by ants after being wounded.

Red-Eye.description: One of Foe-Crusher's five counselors, known for giving advice in critical situations.

Antelope Mountain.description: A place where Cloudy and his retinue are instructed to hide as part of their plan.

banyan tree.description: A large, sacred fig tree native to India, serving as a landmark in the story.

ant-hill.description: A mound built by ants as their nest.

phalanx.description: A compact or close-knit body of people or animals, here referring to the massed ants.

egress.description: An exit or a way out, especially from a fort or enclosure.

fortress.description: A heavily protected and impenetrable building or place.

balk.description: To hesitate or refuse to proceed or to do something.

consort.description: The spouse or companion of a reigning monarch, here referring to the owl-king's mate.

prime minister.description: The chief adviser or minister to a king.

counselors.description: Advisers to a king or ruler.

funeral pile.description: A pyre, a pile of wood for burning a dead body as part of a funeral rite.

snake.description: Snake refers to various serpents in the stories, including the terrifying serpent believed to be the guardian deity of the field, the snake living in an ant-hill, and the snake residing in the prince's belly.

Brahman’s boy.description: The son of the Brahman who attempts to kill the snake for its gold and is killed in return.

dinar.description: An ancient gold coin historically used in India and other regions.

cudgel.description: A short, thick stick used as a weapon.

cremated.description: Burned a dead body to ashes, a common Hindu funerary practice.

lotus.description: A sacred flower in Indian culture, symbolizing purity and spiritual awakening.

Gay-Chariot.description: A king who owns Lotus Lake and must decide a dispute among the golden swans and a great bird.

Lotus Lake.description: A lake owned by King Gay-Chariot, inhabited by golden swans.

kinsmen.description: Relatives or members of the same group; used here for the birds addressing each other.

suppliant.description: One who humbly petitions or begs, especially to someone in authority.

foeman.description: An archaic term for an enemy or adversary.

fowler.description: A bird-catcher who brings harm to forest creatures and is central to the story's events.

dove.description: A self-sacrificing male dove who welcomes the fowler as a guest and ultimately sacrifices himself.

female dove.description: The wife of the dove, who is captured by the fowler and later sacrifices herself to join her husband.

gyves.description: Shackles or fetters used to restrain prisoners.

amain.description: With full force; at full speed.

chariot.description: A vehicle, often horse-drawn, used in ancient India and associated with gods or royalty.

car divine.description: A divine or heavenly chariot, symbolizing ascension to heaven.

brood.description: Offspring or young of an animal, especially birds.

widowhood.description: The state of having lost one's spouse by death.

Lovelorn.description: An aged merchant whose reason was clouded by love; he marries a young woman after his wife's death.

Hangman’s Well.description: A specific well referenced in a simile, associated with pain and death, likely a cultural or legendary location.

maiden.description: An archaic term for a young, unmarried woman.

sue.description: An archaic term meaning to plead or beg.

fain.description: An archaic word meaning gladly or willingly.

bleaching.description: In this context, refers to bones becoming white from exposure, often used in older literature.

driveling.description: Drooling or slobbering, especially as a sign of old age; archaic usage.

doddering.description: Trembling or tottering, typically due to old age.

benefactor.description: Someone who gives help or advantage, often used in moral or didactic tales.

thief.description: A man who plans to steal the Brahman's two cows and becomes entangled with a ghost.

ghost.description: A supernatural being named Truthful who wishes to eat the Brahman.

king.description: A ruler who seeks advice from Wall-Ear.

Truthful.description: The name of the ghost character in this story.

Scriptures.description: Scriptures (including the Vedas and Sacred Word) refer to the sacred Hindu texts that provide religious and moral guidance, often cited as authority in the narrative.

Shibi.description: A legendary king in Indian mythology known for his self-sacrifice.

ointment.description: A smooth substance applied to the skin for medicinal or cosmetic purposes.

betel-gum.description: A preparation made from betel leaves and areca nut, chewed as a stimulant in South Asia.

sacrificial.description: Relating to the act of offering something as a sacrifice, often in a religious context.

ransom.description: A payment made to release someone or something from captivity.

club.description: A heavy stick used as a weapon.

God-like.description: A king in a certain city, father of the prince afflicted by a snake in his belly.

Gift.description: A king in another city who has two daughters and becomes angry at one for her manner of greeting.

prince.description: The son of King God-like, afflicted by a snake living in his belly and later marries a princess.

princess.description: Daughter of King Gift, given in marriage to the prince and helps cure him.

tank.description: An Indian term for a large artificial pond or reservoir, often found near temples or in cities.

alms.description: Charitable donations, usually food or money, given to the poor.

bemire.description: To soil or dirty, often used metaphorically.

deserts.description: A term meaning what one deserves, often in the phrase 'just deserts.'

carpenter.description: A gullible man or Brahman whose wife deceives him through elaborate tricks and infidelity.

wife.description: The unfaithful wife of the carpenter or Brahman who cleverly deceives her husband with stories of goddesses and cakes.

Gauri.description: A divine figure and goddess whose shrine and remedy are invoked in the carpenter's wife's fabricated story.

old lover.description: The wife's former lover, whom she invites to her house while her husband is supposedly away.

whore.description: An archaic and pejorative term for a woman who engages in sexual activity for payment or is considered promiscuous.

proverb.description: A short, commonly known saying that expresses a general truth or piece of advice.

rascal.description: An old-fashioned term for a mischievous or dishonest person.

shrine.description: A place regarded as holy because of its associations with a divinity or a sacred person.

untimely.description: Happening or done at an unsuitable time; premature.

embrace.description: To hold closely in one's arms, especially as a sign of affection.

falsified.description: To make false or incorrect, especially so as to deceive.

uprooted.description: Removed from one's home or usual environment.

corvine.description: Relating to or resembling a crow or raven.

provenience.description: Place of origin or earliest known history of something.

mouse-maid.description: A maiden who is transformed into a mouse, referenced in a fable.

Yajnavalkya.description: The father of the hermitage, a holy man who transforms a mouse into a girl and later arranges her marriage.

sun.description: Personified as a deity and considered for marriage in the story.

cloud.description: Personified as a potential suitor and considered superior to the sun.

wind.description: Personified as a suitor, considered superior to the cloud.

mountain.description: Personified as a suitor, considered superior to the wind.

sacred rites.description: Religious ceremonies or rituals performed for spiritual purposes.

loin-cloth.description: A simple garment worn around the hips, often by ascetics.

raiment.description: An archaic word for clothing or garments.

ceremony of purification.description: A ritual act intended to cleanse a person of spiritual or physical impurities.

nubility.description: The condition of being of marriageable age or suitable for marriage.

spinster.description: An archaic term for an unmarried woman, often used pejoratively.

homage.description: Respect or reverence paid, often in a formal or ritual manner.

viands.description: An archaic word for food or provisions.

hunter.description: A man who traps birds and discovers the bird whose dung turns to gold.

lotus eyes.description: A poetic phrase referring to eyes shaped or beautiful like a lotus, often used in Indian literature to describe beauty.

adherents.description: Followers or supporters, often used in the context of a leader and their loyal companions.

dunderhead.description: An archaic English term for a fool or simpleton.

Rough-Claw.description: A lion who, driven by hunger, hides in a cave to catch prey.

Curd-Face.description: A jackal who owns the cave and cleverly avoids being caught by the lion.

Yudhishthir King.description: The eldest of the Pandava brothers (Pandus), known for his righteousness in the Mahabharata.

Arjun.description: One of the Pandava brothers and a great archer in the Mahabharata, famed for his skill and virtue.

Kunti.description: Mother of the Pandavas in the Mahabharata.

Draupadi.description: Wife of the Pandavas, renowned for her beauty and dignity.

Pot-baking Hell.description: A metaphorical or mythological place of torment, referencing Indian concepts of hell.

Mastya land.description: A reference to the Matsya kingdom from the Mahabharata, where the Pandavas spent time in disguise.

Matsya’s royal court.description: The court of the Matsya kingdom, significant in the Mahabharata.

Virata’s court.description: The court of King Virata, where the Pandavas lived incognito during their exile.

fagot.description: An archaic English term for a bundle of sticks or twigs used for fuel.

pelf.description: Archaic term for money or wealth, often with a negative connotation.

savoir faire.description: French phrase meaning the ability to act appropriately in social situations; here, used to denote social skill.

fawner.description: A person who seeks favor by excessive flattery or obsequious behavior.

Slow-Poison.description: An elderly black snake who devises a cunning plan to make frogs his food by pretending to be cursed and serving as their vehicle.

Water-Foot.description: The frog-king who, along with his counselors and other frogs, rides on Slow-Poison's back, unaware of the snake's true intentions.

palanquin.description: A covered litter for one passenger, carried on poles on the shoulders of several men, used chiefly in eastern Asia.

plebeian.description: Belonging to the common people; lower-class or ordinary, often used in contrast to nobility or elite.

befooled.description: To be deceived or tricked; made a fool of.

plausibilities.description: Statements or actions that seem reasonable or probable, often used to describe deceptive reasoning.

Rama.description: A legendary prince and hero from the Indian epic Ramayana, known for his virtue and exile.

Nala.description: A king from Indian epic literature, known for his misfortunes and adventures.

Bali.description: A mythological king, often associated with the story of Vamana in Hindu mythology.

Lanka’s monster-monarch.description: The demon king of Lanka in the Ramayana, also known as the monster-monarch.

Dasharath.description: The father of Rama in the Ramayana, who became king of heaven after his death.

King Sagar.description: A legendary king in Hindu mythology, known for his attempt to bind the ocean.

Manu.description: The progenitor of mankind in Hindu tradition, sometimes identified with the king Satyavrat.

Mandhatar.description: A legendary king in Hindu mythology, known for his conquests.

Nahush.description: A legendary king who was temporarily king of the gods in Hindu mythology.

Keshav.description: A major deity in Hinduism and leader of the Vrishni clan, also known as Keshav.

kingdom.description: A realm or territory ruled by a king.

bandar-log.description: A term from Indian literature meaning 'monkey people,' popularized by Rudyard Kipling's 'The Jungle Book.'

Lanka.description: The island kingdom ruled by Ravana in the Ramayana.

laving.description: Washing or bathing, especially as part of a ritual.

valor.description: Courage or bravery, especially in battle.

consummation.description: The point at which something is completed or fulfilled.

prudence.description: Wisdom or good judgment in practical matters.

pennons.description: Flags or streamers, especially those carried on a lance.

umbrella.description: A symbol of royalty and protection in Indian culture.

Fate.description: A concept referring to destiny or the predetermined course of events.

cars.description: Archaic term for chariots or vehicles, especially in epic or poetic contexts.
